use: The convent museum documents the plaza façade, paired bell towers, portico, central courtyard galleries, and main circulation.
The national conservation study maps the basilica, raised atrium, terracotta roof ranges and main two-storey cloister.
The municipal heritage authority records the stone front material, stone repairs and remaining ornamental details.
Records three connected churches, loss of one upper belfry stage in 1868 and the 70 m liturgical length to the sacristy.
Documents surviving Chapel of Cantuña and the plaza-side details conserved in 2019.
